chapterNote: The first of the eight closing psalms of David, a thanksgiving with a strange audience: 'before the gods I will sing to You' — in the face of every rival power, real or imagined, David gives thanks to the one God, bowing toward the temple for His covenant love and faithfulness, because God has magnified His word above all His name. The rescue was recent and specific: on the day I called, You answered, and put strength in my soul. Then the horizon widens the way David's thanksgivings always do — all the kings of the earth will thank You when they hear what You have said, and sing of Your ways, because Your glory is great. The center is the LORD's paradox: high, yet He sees the lowly; the proud He knows only from a distance. And the close is a servant's confidence: though I walk in the middle of trouble You revive me; Your hand meets my enemies' anger; Your right hand saves. The LORD will bring to completion what concerns me — so do not let go of the work of Your own hands. Paul's 'He who began a good work in you will complete it' is this verse's New Testament echo.

1.text: Of David. I will give You thanks with my whole heart; in front of the gods I will make music to You.
1.amp: A Psalm of David. I will praise [yadah] You with my whole heart [leb]: before the gods [elohim] will I sing praise [zamar] unto You.
1.notes: odekha be-khol-libbi (H3034, H3820): thanks with the whole heart — Psalm 111:1's opening — neged elohim azammerekka (H430, H2167): in front of the elohim, the gods — whether the idols of the nations or the heavenly court, David's praise is a public defiance of every rival claim.

2.text: I will bow down toward Your holy temple and give thanks to Your name for Your covenant love and Your faithfulness, for You have made Your word great above all Your name.
2.amp: I will worship [shachah — bow low] toward Your holy [qodesh] temple [hekal], and praise [yadah] Your name [shem] for Your lovingkindness [chesed — covenant love] and for Your truth [emeth]: for You have magnified [gadal] Your word [imrah] above all Your name [shem].
2.notes: eshtachaveh el-hekhal qodshekha (H7812, H1964, H6944): bowing toward the sanctuary, the direction of prayer — al-chasdekha ve-al-amittekha (H2617, H571), the Sinai pair. Then the psalm's startling line: higdalta al-kol-shimkha imratekha (H1431, H8034, H565) — Your WORD magnified above all Your NAME: the promise outranks the reputation; God has staked His name on keeping His word.

3.text: The day I called out, You answered me; You put boldness and strength into my soul.
3.amp: In the day [yom] when I cried [qara] You answered [anah] me, and strengthened [rahab — emboldened, made me bold] me with strength [oz] in my soul [nephesh].
3.notes: be-yom qarati va-taaneni (H3117, H7121, H6030): the call and the answer on the same day. tarhibeni be-naphshi oz (H7292, H5315, H5797): rahab is the storm-verb, 'to act boldly' — God made David's soul brazen with strength. Not rescue from the situation first, but courage inside it.

4.text: All the kings of the earth will give You thanks, O LORD, when they hear the words of Your mouth.
4.amp: All the kings [melek] of the earth [eretz] shall praise [yadah] You, O LORD [YHWH], when they hear [shama] the words [emer] of Your mouth [peh].
4.notes: yodukha YHWH kol-malkhe-aretz (H3034, H4428, H776): every king thanking God — ki shameu imre-phikha (H8085, H561, H6310): when they HEAR what He said. The word magnified in verse 2 is the word that will convert thrones; David's private thanksgiving predicts a global one (cf. Psalm 102:15).

5.text: Yes, they will sing about the LORD's ways, for the glory of the LORD is great.
5.amp: Yea, they shall sing [shir] in the ways [derek] of the LORD [YHWH]: for great [gadol] is the glory [kabod] of the LORD.
5.notes: ve-yashiru be-darkhe YHWH (H7891, H1870): kings singing the LORD's ways — His manner of acting, the roads He takes — ki-gadol kebod YHWH (H1419, H3519): because His glory is great, the gadol of verse 2's magnified word.

6.text: For though the LORD is high, He sees the lowly; but the proud He knows only from far away.
6.amp: Though the LORD [YHWH] be high [rum], yet has He respect [raah — sees, regards] unto the lowly [shaphal]: but the proud [gaboah — the lofty] He knows [yada] afar off [merachoq].
6.notes: ki-ram YHWH ve-shaphal yireh (H7311, H8217, H7200): the paradox of Psalm 113 — high, and He sees the low. ve-gaboah mi-merachaq yeyeda (H1364, H4801, H3045): the lofty He knows from a distance — the same yada that means intimate knowledge, withheld: God keeps the proud at arm's length (cf. James 4:6; Isaiah 57:15).

7.text: Though I walk in the very midst of trouble, You keep me alive; You stretch out Your hand against the anger of my enemies, and Your right hand saves me.
7.amp: Though I walk [yalak] in the midst [qereb] of trouble [tsarah], You will revive [chayah — keep alive, restore] me: You shall stretch forth [shalach] Your hand [yad] against the wrath [aph] of mine enemies [oyeb], and Your right hand [yamin] shall save [yasha] me.
7.notes: im-elekh be-qereb tsarah techayyeni (H3212, H7130, H6869, H2421): Psalm 23:4's valley, with chayah — You keep me alive — instead of 'I fear no evil'. al-aph oyevai tishlach yadekha (H639, H341, H7971, H3027): Your hand sent against their anger; ve-toshieni yeminekha (H3467, H3225): the right hand, the saving one. Two hands of God, one blocking and one rescuing.

8.text: The LORD will bring to completion what concerns me; Your covenant love, O LORD, endures forever — do not let go of the work of Your own hands.
8.amp: The LORD [YHWH] will perfect [gamar — complete, finish] that which concerns me: Your mercy [chesed — covenant love], O LORD, endures for ever [olam]: forsake [raphah — let go, slacken] not the works [maaseh] of Your own hands [yad].
8.notes: YHWH yigmor baadi (H1584): the LORD will FINISH for me — gamar, Psalm 57:2's verb; Philippians 1:6 is this line's New Testament echo. YHWH chasdekha le-olam (H2617, H5769), the Great Hallel's refrain; then the plea that ends the psalm: maase yadekha al-teref (H4639, H3027, H7503) — do not let go of what Your hands made. A servant asking the Craftsman to keep His grip on the piece.
